title: OME · Multi-cluster control plane
description: Health of the multi-cluster control plane: the placer and the quota plane, each with its own health, resource and behaviour panels. Generic signals only — see the coverage-limits panel for what is deliberately absent.

panels.title: WorkloadClusters
panels.description: Members registered with each control plane -- the fleet this plane places onto. A count only: whether a member is reachable is not exported anywhere. The Ready condition exists on the CR but no metric carries it, so a member that has been unreachable for hours still counts here.

panels.title: InferenceServices (all namespaces)
panels.description: Live object count from the apiserver, across all namespaces. A count, not a state breakdown: Ready vs failed vs in-progress is not available here.

panels.title: Ready
panels.description: From kube-state-metrics, so it still reports when the pod is down and therefore exporting nothing. available < desired is the signal.

panels.title: Leader (must be 1)
panels.description: The gauge is 1 on the leader and 0 on each follower, so a correct sum is 1 at any replica count. Reading 2 means the pod is being collected twice, not that there are two leaders.

panels.title: Container restarts (1h)
panels.description: Neither Deployment carries a PodDisruptionBudget or a priorityClassName, so eviction and OOM-kill surface here first.

panels.title: CPU (cores)
panels.description: Absolute cores, one line per replica -- 1 means one core fully used. Taken from the process rather than cAdvisor because a container-name selector also matches unrelated operators that call their container "manager".

panels.title: Memory (RSS)
panels.description: One line per replica. Growth tracks the informer caches, which on a control plane scale with members x derived objects. A single replica climbing while its peers stay flat is the leader doing the work.

panels.title: Reconcile rate by controller
panels.description: A controller with no activity in the window drops out rather than drawing a line at zero.

panels.title: Outcome mix (placement)
panels.description: requeue and requeue_after dominating with no success is retrying without converging.

panels.title: Reconcile errors
panels.description: There is no error taxonomy: every failure class collapses into this counter. The class is recoverable only from the Event reason or the logs.

panels.title: Reconcile latency p99
panels.description: Bounded by whatever timeout the pass runs under, so a wedged remote dependency reads as a normal-length pass. Read it with the outcome mix.

panels.title: Oldest unfinished work
panels.description: The stall detector. A monotonically climbing line is a wedged worker -- the failure mode the probes cannot catch, because neither checks reconcile progress.

panels.title: Queue wait p99
panels.description: Time an item waits for a worker, as distinct from the time the work then takes. Rising wait with flat work duration is backpressure.

panels.title: Worker saturation
panels.description: Busy workers over the configured ceiling. These controllers run at MaxConcurrentReconciles=1, so one slow pass blocks the queue and this pins at 1 for as long as it lasts.

panels.title: Apiserver calls by code
panels.description: 409 is a status-write conflict, which is how contention between two writers of the same object shows up.

panels.title: Webhook requests by code
panels.description: Flat zero is expected where the role disables its webhooks. Denials are not visible here either way: a rejection is HTTP 200 with allowed=false, so it is indistinguishable from an approval.

panels.title: What this board cannot tell you, and the fix for each

options.content:
Every panel above is a generic signal — controller-runtime, kube-state-metrics, or the apiserver. Neither the placement stack nor the quota stack registers a custom metric, so this board shows both processes are *running*, never that either is *correct*.

| Gap | Why it is missing | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| InferenceService state — Ready, failed, in-progress, per namespace | The platform kube-state-metrics on a management cluster carries no OME `customResourceState` config, so every `ome_inferenceservice_*` series is absent. Only the raw object count above exists. | Add `config/monitoring/kube-state-metrics-config.yaml` to that KSM. Config only, no OME code change. |
| Quota **correctness** — projection lag per member, chips nominal vs admitted vs borrowed, admission decisions by denial reason, tree structural health | The quota plane is scraped now, but `pkg/quota` registers no metrics of its own, so its row is entirely controller-runtime: it shows the loop turning, never that the numbers it produces are right. | Instrument `pkg/quota`. The raw values largely exist already — `status.clusters[]` carries applied-vs-materialized generations, and the capacity pass computes an unattributed figure it then discards. |
| Whether quota accounting matches reality | Kueue does not gate serving pods on this fleet, so admitted counts read zero while accelerators are consumed. Every usage metric added today would read a healthy zero. | A pod-derived consumption metric split by whether Kueue governs the pod, so the two cases stop looking alike. |
| The single-active invariant — two members serving one InferenceService | No metric, no event, no condition. The loser sweep returns void and swallows per-member failures. | Placement instrumentation. |
| Per-member health | `WorkloadCluster.status.conditions[Ready]` is the only signal, is not exported to Prometheus, and reports True for the whole connection grace window while the member is already failing its probe. | A KSM `customResourceState` entry for WorkloadCluster, or placement instrumentation. |
| Fan-out latency, race outcome, sweep lag, derived-object reaping | Computed by `tests/perf/multicluster` offline and nowhere in production. | Instrumentation. |

Nothing on this board can page anyone: `prometheusRule.enabled` is false everywhere, no PrometheusRule object is deployed, and Alertmanager has no route or receiver.

*The `cluster` variable is scoped to control planes running the placer, so a new tier appears here as soon as it is deployed, with no dashboard change.*
